text:
nina - AE: Customer (PulseMed) wants a short Private POC. They have hybrid setup: onprem inference + multi-account AWS. Primary asks: recommend connectivity (PrivateLink vs VPC peering vs transit), any TLS inspect caveats, and a tight POC cost estimate.

cal - solutions eng: Quick guidance: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is our default for cross-account isolated access — less routing complexity and simpler IAM/endpoint policies. VPC peering can work inside same account or peered accounts but exposes routing/state and doesn't scale well for many spokes. Transit (TGW) fits large-scale multi-VPC topologies and preserves source IPs more naturally if you control routing. For latency, per-AZ PrivateLink ENIs are usually the lowest hop count.

diego - netops: Operational notes: PrivateLink requires an ENI per AZ — confirm they enable cross-account endpoints if necessary. Peering requires route table entries and careful overlapping-CIDR checks. If they use an onprem proxy that terminates TLS (DLP), mutual-TLS will fail. Streaming caveat: TLS-terminating proxies can buffer/chunk and break server-sent streaming; advise passthrough for streaming endpoints.

mei - security: Security checklist we can provide: SOC2 type II attestation, TLS 1.3 by default, option for customer-managed KMS in Private, audit log exports to their S3, and SCIM/SAML integration. For TLS inspect: recommend creating a bypass for our ENI CIDRs or interface endpoint DNS to avoid MITM on client cert chains.

diego - netops: Minimal firewall snippet they can paste (replace CIDRs with the list we'll send):
```
- proto: tcp
  ports: [443]
  dest_cidr: ["10.50.60.0/28","10.50.61.0/28"]
  description: "Allow Redwood Private deploy ENIs"
# For streaming/websocket: allow ephemeral ports outgoing if you have a proxy
- proto: tcp
  ports: [1024-65535]
  dest_fqdn: ["connect.redwood.api"]
```
Also: to preserve client src IP for logging, avoid SNAT between app subnets and ENI, or use 1:1 NAT.

nina - AE: They pressed on cost: 7-day POC, ~12TB egress, multi-AZ. Give a ballpark we can show them quickly.

cal - solutions eng: Ballpark (region dependent): PrivateLink endpoint ~$0.015/hr per endpoint + data processing ~$0.01/GB. For 12TB (~12,000GB) data processing ~ $120. If using 3 AZ endpoints for HA: 3 * 24 * 7 * $0.015 =~ $7.6. Total POC network add-on ~$130. If they use TGW with heavy cross-AZ transfer, costs can rise due to inter-AZ and NAT egress — for sustained >20TB/month evaluate dedicated transit pricing. Note: GPU/dedicated capacity pricing separate.

mei - security: We'll prepare a short answers doc for their security questionnaire including network diagrams, KMS flow, and a TLS-inspect recommendation. If legal wants a data-flow annex, I can draft it.

diego - netops: Action: uploading exact ENI CIDR list + sample iptables SNAT bypass snippet to ticket PM-POC-77 by 1600 PT.

cal - solutions eng: I'll attach a 2-row cost sketch (PrivateLink vs TGW) with conservative numbers to the ticket.

nina - AE: Great. I'll share the artifacts with PulseMed and schedule a 30min call to review TLS inspect implications. billing-bot: create POC estimate record.

billing-bot: POC estimate created: POCE-9921. Link: https://billing.redwood.ai/POCE-9921

mei - security: Quick FYI: If PulseMed wants encrypted inspection at their DLP, we strongly prefer a passthrough rule for our endpoints or mutual-TLS end-to-end; else some features (streaming, client cert auth) may be unavailable.

nina - AE: Thanks everyone 44d
